Date Dec....15th, 1939.

Subject (in full) Alleged new Anti-Japanese Chinese Women's Group in existance
in Footung Bank Building.
Made by.... S. I. Kao Yen-keng....Forwarded by.... D. I. Crawford

With reference to the attached translation
of an article appearing in the Mainchi dated Dec. 7
on a subject of a new anti-Japanese "Shanghai Women's
Special Service Group" operating on the third floor
of the Footung Bank Building, 130 Avenue Edward VII,
enquiries show that the Footung Bank Building is
actually situated at 274 Avenue Edward VII and that
nothing is known of the alleged group and its
organizer Naoh Chi-sung ( 岳澤生 ) on the third
floor. Discreet enquiries at the Siang Yao (湘姚)
Supplementary School in Room 31 & 37 also failed
to confirm the report that secret meetings of Chinese
women and girl students are held there.

D. C. (Special Branch)

WOMEN'S SPECIAL SERVICE CORPS RESPONSIBLE FOR
SHOOTING OF SECRETARY OF CHINESE WOMEN'S CLUB

As Miss Mau Li Ying, age 28,
Secretary of the Shanghai Women's Club, in company with
two friends, was walking down the stairs of the Club on
the first floor of Hall & Holtz Company at the corner
of Nanking and Szechuen Roads at about 7. p.m. December 12
she was fired at by two Chinese desperadoes who made good
their escape after they had shot her down.
Various theories have been
advanced regarding the motive of the crime because
the victim is a young girl. However, as a result
of an investigation conducted by the authorities
concerned it was learned that the Shanghai Women's
Special Service Corps is responsible for the crime.
The Shanghai Women's Special
Service Corps was established on the second floor
of the Pootung Guild Building at No. 274 Avenue
Edward VII, International Settlement side, towards
the end of October by Dien Soh Chuin, wife of General
Yang Fu, a former Woosung-Shanghai Defence Commissioner,
and Yao Nyoh Lan, wife of Doo Yuch Sun, leader of
the Green Pang, on the instructions of Ngoh Cheh Sun,
officer in charge of the Shanghai office of the Chung-
king Government.
At 4 p.m. December 12 a member
of the Shanghai Women's Special Service Corps called
on Mau Li Ying to ask her to join the Corps. They
had a talk lasting for about 2 hours. After the member
of the Special Service Corps had left, Mau was attacked
as she was leaving the Club with two friends.
The Special Service Corps is
said to have engineered the outrage because she had
refused to become a member of the Corps.

妇女特种服务队应对中国妇女俱乐部秘书被枪击事件负责

12月12日晚7时许，28岁的上海妇女俱乐部秘书毛丽英小姐与两位朋友一起，走在南京路与四川路拐角处霍尔茨公司一楼俱乐部的楼梯上时，遭到两名中国暴徒的枪击，暴徒在将其击倒后成功逃脱。
由于受害者是一名年轻女子，关于犯罪动机出现了各种推测。然而，经有关当局调查得知，上海妇女特种服务队应对此罪行负责。
上海妇女特种服务队由前吴淞-上海防卫专员杨虎将军的妻子丁佐中（Dien Soh Chuin，音译）和青帮首领杜月笙的妻子姚玉兰（Yao Nyoh Lan，音译），根据重庆政府上海办事处负责人吴铁城（Ngoh Cheh Sun，音译）的指示，于10月底在国际租界一侧爱多亚路274号浦东同乡会二楼成立。
12月12日下午4时，上海妇女特种服务队的一名成员拜访了毛丽英，邀请她加入该队。她们交谈了约2小时。在该特种服务队成员离开后，毛丽英在与两位朋友离开俱乐部时遭到袭击。
据说，特种服务队策划此次暴行是因为她拒绝成为该队成员。

OFF THE RECORD . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . NEWS BEHIND
                                                                                                          THE. NEWS

Mata Hari Harem
GREATLY worried over a Mata Hari harem
here, which, according to official informa-
tion is another mirage of the publishers, the
Japanese and a section of the puppet press
have reported the formation here of an Anti-
Japanese Chinese Women's Association.
There seems to be nothing secret about this un-
usual spy ring which has its own Special Service
section The Mainichi even announced details re-
garding this "gang," stating that the women met in
a room on the third floor of the Pootung Guild, 130
Avenue Edward VII. More than 130 prominent Chi-
nese women in the foreign-administered areas are
members of this group, the Japanese paper alleged.
However, the paper failed to explain just why the
Japanese authorities, who have demanded the ran-
sacking of houses and even did so illegally them-
selves whenever they thought anti-Japanese acti-
vities were proceeding at any address, did not
search this particular headquarters of the female
espionage ring.
The Mainichi has everything down pat,
too:
"Chiang Kai-shek sent the sum of $150,000
to Naoh Chih-sung, officer in charge of the
Shanghai Office of the Chungking Govern-
ment." (Nobody knows who this mysterious
Nach is.) The paper, however, claims he is
holding the fund to cover the expenses of the
women's activities.
Whoever this mysterious head of the Mata Hari
Harem is, the Mainichi claims that he receives aid
from Mrs. Dien Tso-chung, "wife of General Yang
Ho." General Yang Ho, it will be recalled, was the
former commander of the Woosung Garrison, but
nobody knows that his wife is in town, or that her
name was Dien Tso-chung.
The activities of these women, the paper finally
admits, largely consists of bribing publications and
enrolling members at "public" meetings.
Imagine our Mata Haris going around enrolling
members into their secret organizations at public
meetings.

《字林西报》

1939年12月10日

非官方记录 ____ 新闻背后的新闻

玛塔·哈里后宫
日本人和部分傀儡报纸报道在此成立了一个反日中国妇女协会，据官方消息，这不过是出版商制造的另一个海市蜃楼，但他们对此处的“玛塔·哈里后宫”深感担忧。
这个不同寻常的间谍网似乎没有什么秘密可言，它拥有自己的特种服务部门。《每日新闻》甚至公布了关于这个“帮派”的细节，称这些妇女在爱多亚路130号浦东同乡会三楼的一个房间里聚会。该日文报纸声称，有130多名居住在外国管理区的知名中国女性是该组织的成员。
然而，该报未能解释为何日本当局没有搜查这个女性间谍网的特定总部，尽管他们只要认为任何地址有反日活动，就要求搜查房屋，甚至非法亲自进行搜查。
《每日新闻》对细节也了如指掌：
“蒋介石向重庆政府上海办事处负责人岳志松（Naoh Chih-sung，音译）汇去15万美元。”（没人知道这个神秘的岳是谁。）但该报声称他持有这笔资金以支付妇女活动的费用。
无论这个神秘的“玛塔·哈里后宫”头目是谁，《每日新闻》声称他得到杨虎将军妻子丁佐中（Dien Tso-chung，音译）的援助。众所周知，杨虎将军是前吴淞卫戍司令，但没人知道他的夫人在本市，也没人知道她的名字叫丁佐中。
该报最后承认，这些妇女的活动主要包括贿赂出版物和在“公开”会议上招募成员。
想象一下，我们的玛塔·哈里们在公开会议上四处奔波，将成员招募进她们的秘密组织。

MAINICHI. 7.12.39

CHIANG KAI SHEK ISSUES LARGE SUM OF MONEY TO NEW
ANTI-JAPANESE CHINESE WOMEN'S GROUP IN
FOREIGN SETTLEMENTS.

Acting on information that Chinese women of
the educated class and Chinese girl students are fre [u]enting
a room on the third floor of the Pootung Guild, No. [5]0
Avenue Edward VII. to hold secret meetings, the authorities
made an investigation and discovered a secret meeting place
which was used at the same time as the office of the Special
Service Section of the newly organized Anti-Japanese Chinese
Women's Association, a body organized by about 130 important
Chinese women residing in the Foreign Settlements.
Towards the end of October, 1939, Chiang Kai
Shek issued secret instructions and a sum of $150,000 to
Naoh Chih Sung, the officer in charge of the Shanghai Office
of the Chungking Government, to cover the expenses of
the women's activities.

With the co-operation of Dien Tso Chung, wife
of General Yang Fu, the former Woosung-Shanghai Defence
Commissioner, and Yao Siu Cheu, wife of Tu Yueh Sun, the
leader of the Green Pang, Naoh Chi Sung succeeded in
assembling about 130 Chinese women of the educated class.
About the middle of last month, these women
formed a Shanghai Women's Special Service Group with
an office on the third floor of the Pootung Guild.
This Special Service Group is actively engaged in anti-
Japanese propaganda work by bribing publications and
enrolling members at public meetings.

《每日新闻》 1939年12月7日

蒋介石向外国租界内新的反日中国妇女团体提供巨额资金

根据受过教育的中国女性和中国女学生频繁前往爱多亚路[5]0号浦东同乡会三楼的一个房间举行秘密会议的情报，当局进行了调查，发现了一个秘密集会地点，该地点同时用作新成立的反日中国妇女协会特种服务处的办公室，该协会由约130名居住在外侨居留地的知名中国女性组成。
1939年10月底，蒋介石向重庆政府上海办事处负责人岳志松（Naoh Chih Sung，音译）发出秘密指示并提供15万美元，用于支付妇女活动的费用。
在前吴淞-上海防卫专员杨虎将军的妻子丁佐中（Dien Tso Chung，音译）和青帮首领杜月笙的妻子姚筱珠（Yao Siu Cheu，音译）的合作下，岳志松成功召集了约130名受过教育的中国女性。
上月月中旬，这些妇女成立了上海妇女特种服务团，办事处设在浦东同乡会三楼。
该特种服务团通过贿赂出版物和在公开会议上招募成员，积极从事反日宣传工作。

Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C Crawford

Under the auspices of the Chung Hwa Women's Mutual
Aid Society, Room 605, Pootung Guild, 1454 Ave. Edward
VII, a play entitled "The Devil of Desire" was staged
in the Strand Theatre, 586 Ningpo Road, between 9 a.m.
and 11.10 a.m. July 13, when some 700 persons attended.
A total of some $200.00 was raised through the sale of
admission tickets and will be used for the establishment
of a free supplementary school for women.

During the proceedings, copies of a pamphlets
containing synopsis of the play and articles on the pro-
ject of the society to establish a free supplementary
school for women, were distributed to the attendance.
Drafts of these articles were submitted on July 10
to this Branch for examination. They contain nothing
of an objectionable nature.

Subject Chung Hwa Women's Mutual Aid Society - to hold theatrical
performances in Strand Theatre.
Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien, Forwarded by C. Clausen.

The Chung Hwa Women's Mutual Aid Society, Room
605, Pootung Guild, 1454 Avenue Edward VII, proposes to
stage a play entitled "The Devil of Desire" (慾魔) on
the forenoon of July 13, 1939 in the Strand Theatre,
586 Ningpo Road, for the purpose of raising funds to
meet expenses for the establishment of a Free Women's
Supplementary School and has arranged a rehearsal on
the forenoon of July 1. 1939 in the same theatre. A
total of 1,200 admission tickets priced at $0.40 and
$0.60 each, and 35 honorary tickets priced at $5.00
each have been prepared by the society and will be
distributed to the members for sale among their friends
and relatives.

A letter addressed to the Municipal Police and
another to the Council by the society applying for
permission to stage the play were received on 1/7/39
and 5/7/39 respectively and are attached hereto together
with translation.

The synopsis of the play entitled "The Devil of
Desire" which is on the subject of love and marriage
has been examined and found to contain nothing of an
objectionable nature.

The Chung Hwa Women's Mutual Aid Society was

sources tends to show that she has confined herself to
activities that are in no way connected with anti-Japanese
activity. While it is true that her movements are very
discreet and her present address is only known to a few of
her personal confidants, she is more or less justified in
adopting this precautionary measure in view of her previous

FORMER WOOSUNG-SHANGHAI DEFENCE COMMISSIONER'S
WIFE ARRIVES IN SHANGHAI TO REVIVE ANTI-
JAPANESE WOMEN'S ORGANIZATION

According to information reaching
a certain quarter on December 4, Dien Pih Chuin, wife of
a former Woosung-Shanghai Defence Commissioner, was
actively engaged, on instructions from Soong Mei Ling, in
directing anti-Japanese movements in Shanghai after the
outbreak of hostilities. Since the fall of Hankow her
activities ceased because she could not get into touch
with all the staff officers of anti-Japanese organizations.
She later proceeded to Hongkong on a British steamer,
thence to Chungking where she lived together with Soong
Mei Ling.
On instructions from Soong Mei
Ling she came to Shanghai in the beginning of November
to revive the Anti-Japanese Women's National Salvation
Association. She is now living on Route Ferguson, French
Concession. She was given a sum of money by Soong Mei
Ling for this work but the amount will not be sufficient
for the purpose. She is endeavouring to get into
touch with all anti-Japanese organizations.
